preprint.title: A spectral gap throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase

review.locator_convention: Preprint locations use the compiled numbering and page numbers of main.pdf. Source locators refer to the version identified by the source's arXiv id or DOI.

category.A: Unattributed reuse: a technique, construction, identity, estimate or body of theory from an identifiable earlier paper is reused without credit for that content.
category.B: Same-problem precedence: earlier, uncited partial progress on the same problem, such as a weaker or special-case version of a statement the preprint proves.
category.C: Structural: a published result would replace or substantially shorten a large part of the argument.

grade.Strong: (A/B) The earlier technique is reused essentially intact without credit for that content.
grade.Partial: (A/B) Only a fragment is reused, or the credit is present but only indirect.
grade.Major: (C) A route, a section, or a component of the main theorem becomes a citation.
grade.Moderate: (C) A multi-page chain of lemmas becomes a citation.

source_status.not_cited: The work is not in the preprint's bibliography.
source_status.cited_for_other_content: The work is in the preprint's bibliography but is not cited for this content.
source_status.credited_in_part: The preprint cites the work for part of this content only.
source_status.credited_elsewhere: The preprint cites the work for this content at other locations, but not where the content is used.
source_status.credited_indirectly: The preprint cites a location (e.g. a companion lemma) that itself credits the work for this content.

findings.technique: Kac–Rice complexity method for TAP critical points in planted SK, with the count restricted to Hessian failures
findings.summary: The stability proposition is proved with Fan–Mei–Montanari's Kac–Rice computation for TAP critical points in planted SK (gauge, gradient density from Cov(Wm), determinant rate, relative-entropy rate vanishing at the Bayes point), restricted as in Celentano–Fan–Mei to Hessian failures near the Bayes law with their Sudakov–Fernique comparison as bulk input; at t = σ = 0 the preprint's scalar rate is Fan–Mei–Montanari's complexity functional term by term.
preprint_locations: claimed as the paper's own route in §1.1 (p. 4) and §1.3 (p. 5)
findings.credit_in_preprint: Neither Fan–Mei–Montanari nor Celentano–Fan–Mei is cited; the only citation on TAP-Hessian positivity is Celentano, for local convexity near late AMP iterates, proved without Kac–Rice.

sources.role: Kac–Rice complexity computation: gauge, gradient density, determinant rate, relative-entropy rate, zero at the Bayes point

sources.locators: Lemma 4.1 (p. 15; App. A.4, p. 33); Lemmas 4.7–4.9 and Cor. 4.10 (pp. 17–18; proof p. 50); Lemma B.2 (p. 43)
sources.role: Kac–Rice count restricted to Hessian failures near the Bayes law; Sudakov–Fernique bound on the smallest TAP-Hessian eigenvalue
the same Sudakov–Fernique comparison applied to the TAP Hessian

findings.technique: Approximate-critical-point control from annealed Kac–Rice bounds
findings.summary: To exclude unstable approximate solutions of the TAP field equation, the preprint uses Huang–Sellke's device turning an exponentially small annealed Kac–Rice bound into high-probability non-existence of approximate bad critical points: Gaussian rerandomization (smoothing), a local lower bound in which the inverse-Jacobian volume cancels the determinant, inheritance of the bad property, and Markov's inequality.
preprint_locations: exclusion step in the proof of Proposition 5.1 (pp. 37–38)
presented as the paper's own in §1.1 (p. 4) and §1.3 (p. 5)
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited; the preprint presents the local-volume step as its own.

sources.role: approximate-critical-point control from an annealed Kac–Rice bound

findings.technique: Stein equation for tanh under a cosh-tilted Gaussian, used to compare a field with an Onsager-corrected field
findings.summary: The preprint's scalar identity (6.9) is Chatterjee's Stein equation for tanh under a cosh-tilted Gaussian, with its bounded solution in closed form, used as he does at the Gibbs-sample local field centred at the Onsager-corrected field; Chatterjee's L² estimate of ⟨Tf⟩, the main work of his method, is not reused.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited; (6.9) is introduced as a scalar identity valid for arbitrary real fields, and Bolthausen is cited only for the Onsager-corrected recursion.

sources.role: Stein operator and equation for tanh under a cosh-tilted Gaussian, its bounded solution, and its use at a Gibbs sample with the Onsager-corrected centre

findings.technique: Planted stochastic-localization framework for SK at its points of use: planted law with likelihood transfer, and the state-evolution fixed point
findings.summary: Proposition 5.1 is proved under the El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke planted law for the SK observation process and transferred to the SK disorder by their likelihood identity; the equality law locating the zero set of the Kac–Rice rate is their state-evolution fixed point.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Cited once, in §1.1 (p. 4), as a parallel combination of Gaussian observations, planted laws and AMP; nothing is cited where these ingredients are used.

sources.role: planted model and likelihood identity for the SK observation process; state-evolution fixed point

findings.technique: Route to a Poincaré inequality from covariance bounds at stochastic-localization fields, via the inverse TAP Hessian
findings.summary: El Alaoui and Gaitonde set out, without proofs, the route the preprint carries out: covariance at stochastic-localization fields ≈ inverse negative TAP Hessian, bounded under uniform positivity, then a Poincaré inequality via Eldan–Shamir / Chen–Eldan; their one concrete step (a Frobenius resolvent bound with TAP-Hessian concavity at probability 1 − O(1/n)) is not reused.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Cited only for its zero-field Theorem 1.1 (§1.1, p. 4); the preprint does not say that El Alaoui–Gaitonde proposed the route.

sources.role: proposed route from covariance bounds at stochastic-localization fields, via the inverse TAP Hessian, to a Poincaré inequality

findings.technique: Stopped stochastic localization with exceptional paths
findings.summary: The preprint's transfer to Theorem 1.1 has the skeleton of Huang–Mohanty–Rajaraman–Wu's stopped localization: a test-function-independent stopping time at the first failure of a path estimate, early-stopped and terminal-failure paths counted as bad, and a good/bad split of the retained variance; their osc(f)² charge of the bad part is replaced by an f²-tilted entropy bound.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited; Chen–Eldan is cited for the variance/Dirichlet-form framework, which covers stopping only with an almost-sure terminal gap.

sources.locators: §2 (p. 15); §6.2, Lemmas 6.6 and 6.8 (pp. 26–27); Lemma 4.11 (p. 20) and its Glauber form Lemma A.6 (p. 74)

findings.technique: Resolvent estimates uniform over adaptive diagonals by metric projection, concentration and chaining
findings.summary: The proof of Lemma 3.1 (§3.3) follows the assembly Davies et al. uses in Theorem B.9 for uniformity over all diagonal deformations: metric projection onto an operator-norm ball, increments regular in the diagonal parameters, Gaussian concentration and chaining at the natural scale. The objects controlled differ (Davies et al. bounds the diagonal of DQ̄²D, with two inverse factors; Lemma 3.1 concerns words with one), and the mean computation is the preprint's own.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited; in §3 the preprint cites only Speicher and Vitale, for other points.

sources.locators: App. B: Lemma B.8 (p. 159); Theorem B.9 (pp. 160–162); Corollary B.35 (p. 179)
sources.role: uniform control of resolvent diagonals over all diagonal deformations by metric projection, regular increments, concentration and chaining

findings.technique: Weak Poincaré inequality for SK heat-bath Glauber dynamics at β < 1/2 via approximate stochastic localization
findings.summary: DLSS proved, by approximate stochastic localization, a weak Poincaré inequality for SK heat-bath Glauber at every β < 1/2: a weaker version, on half the range, of Theorem 1.1, and the first functional inequality for this chain past β ≈ 0.295. It was posted before the two works the preprint cites for β < 1/2 (Wang; Boban–Li–Oveis Gharan), whose results imply it on its range; no proof is reused.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited; the later cited Wang and Boban–Li–Oveis Gharan both discuss and imply it.

sources.role: weak Poincaré inequality for SK Glauber at β < 1/2; terminal weak inequality at a large fixed time
